subject: Edge streaming SLO qualification and pilot buy criteria
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: Edge streaming SLO qualification and pilot buy criteria

Tara — thanks again for the demo this morning. Putting a short, actionable recap here so we have a shared baseline for the pilot and procurement asks. Please confirm the highlighted numbers and any missing constraints.

Key asks / confirmed requirements (from today's session):
- Latency: p95 <= 200ms for streaming responses up to 512 tokens; p99 target for critical paths <= 400ms.
- Throughput: baseline 350 requests/minute, burst to 1200 rpm for short windows (<= 2 min).
- Concurrency: sustained concurrency target 15–20 sessions, peak bursts to 60.
- Streaming: client must receive first token within 50–80ms after request start; support for chunked streaming (server-sent).
- Model: open-model family (LLM-X v2 7B quantized) — we validated functional parity in demo.
- Security: TLS + mutual auth for Private deployment; audit logs retention 1 year.

Pilot proposal (high level):
- 2-week streaming pilot in Redwood Dedicated (US region) with autoscaling guardrails.
- Load profile: 48-hour soak + 2 controlled spike windows to validate burst behavior.
- Acceptance criteria: p95 latency within 200ms for 512-token streams; no more than 1% dropped streams; continuous concurrency handling at 20 sessions for 2 hours.

Open items for you:
1) Confirm burst tolerance window (we assumed 2 minutes above).
2) Confirm whether TLS mutual auth is required for pilot or only for production.
3) Any additional network egress restrictions (IP allowlist only, or VPC peering needed?).

Attachments: edge-slo-checklist-v1.xlsx (SLO table + measurement plan). I also attached a stub quote for Dedicated capacity — if we agree on pilot scope I'll update with exact instance sizing.

Next actionable steps:
- You confirm the three open items and sign-off on the pilot scope (we can do that by reply).
- Redwood to provide pilot runbook and updated quote (Ben will own pricing).
- Kickoff: propose Mon 2028-02-21 for a short pilot kickoff call.

Thanks —

From: Tara Singh <tara@edgeailabs.com>

Cc: devops@edgeailabs.com
Date: Wed, 15 Feb 2028 09:04:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Edge streaming SLO qualification and pilot buy criteria

Karthik — thanks for the clear recap and for the demo follow-up. We're aligned on most of this; a couple clarifications below.

Quick clarifications:
- Burst window: we typically allow ~3 minutes for spikes coming from synchronous API bursts (client-side fan-out). Can you size the autoscaling to tolerate 3-minute spikes to 1,200 rpm?
- TLS mutual auth: required for production. For the pilot we can do strong TLS (mTLS preferred but optional) — we will need a short checklist on how Redwood obtains certs or whether we provide them.
- Network: we'll start with IP allowlist for the pilot but will likely require VPC peering for production.

Developer note: devops@edgeailabs.com copied — they will send our network diagram and the load-profile CSV later today (attached). Also, we have a hard requirement that end-to-end time to first token for streaming must be reproducible during our internal load tests (we need reproducibility to run our regression harness).

One more ask on acceptance criteria: can Redwood provide a short-run (1 hr) smoke test plan we can run internally to validate first-token latency before the pilot? If yes, include it in the runbook.

Appreciate it —
Tara Singh
Head of Platform Engineering, EdgeAI Labs
tara@edgeailabs.com

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 16 Feb 2028 13:21:00 +0000
Subject: Internal: Pilot sizing recommendations for EdgeAI Labs

Internal note — copying here so we're aligned before I respond to Tara with technical detail. High-level recommendations based on the numbers:

Recommended pilot config:
- Dedicated pool: 4 x A100-LG (or equivalent) with mixed batching enabled; initial reserved capacity to handle 350 rpm sustained + caching for prefixes.
- Autoscaling: scale up policy to add 2 instances within 90s when 75% CPU or 60% GPU mem pressure for sustained 60s; burst allowance to hit 1200 rpm for up to 3 minutes by spinning up ephemeral burst nodes (pre-warmed).
- KV/prefix caching: enable client-side prefix hints and server-side KV cache to reduce re-computation on repeated prompts. That will help first-token latency under concurrency.
- Streaming: use low-latency kernel path and prioritize first-token emission — optimize chunk size to 32 tokens for initial streams.

Risks / things to validate in pilot:
1) Network variance from EdgeAI's side (packet loss, proxy timeout) — include p99 path latency baseline.
2) mTLS integration steps — ask SRE for cert distribution approach; if they want us to provide certs we'll need a short lead time.
3) Observability: add token-level breakdowns to pilot dashboards (first-token, median generation, token emission tail).

I'll draft the smoke-test steps and a short load driver script snippet. Ben — can you attach an updated Dedicated quote with the 4x A100-LG baseline and burst pricing? I'll include both in the runbook.

Soojin Lee
